decisions.reason: The carpentry workshop is somewhat costlier and more market-exposed than core care services, but it still fits the firm's sheltered-workshop and training capabilities well enough to keep this option open for further learning.
Outpatient sociotherapy is very close to the firm's core portfolio, relatively scalable, and inexpensive to continue while demand and referral potential become clearer.
Counseling for senior living is highly aligned with the firm's eldercare expertise, low in fixed-cost exposure, and strategically attractive to retain as a gateway into other services.
The retail shop remains the most peripheral and commercially uncertain option, and after an additional period its likely learning value no longer justifies tying up attention and operating resources.

Meal delivery for seniors is close to the established eldercare offer and worth retaining as a newer option, even though logistics and staffing make its economics less certain than advisory or therapeutic services.
